sources.title: OpenAI · GPT-6.1 Sol
sources.note: Current model capabilities and standard token pricing. Candidate for concise cloud coaching; no sleep-specific evaluation has been run.

sources.title: OpenAI · Structured Outputs
sources.note: Schema-constrained output can shape a routine or brief. Application validation must still check every value and action.

sources.title: Anthropic · Current model catalog
sources.note: Sonnet 5.5 is a balanced challenger; the catalog also includes Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. Bigger models are optional evaluation candidates, not automatic upgrades.

sources.title: Google · Gemini model catalog
sources.note: Lists Gemini 4 Argon, 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Live as stable. Different models serve reasoning, responsive summaries and spoken interaction.

sources.title: Google · What’s new in Gemini 4 Argon
sources.note: Current flagship supports tunable reasoning. Introductory pricing ends 30 November 2026; evaluate quality and full reasoning-token cost before adopting.

sources.title: Google · Live API
sources.note: Realtime audio makes an optional spoken check-in feasible. It adds microphone, connection and audio-retention decisions.

sources.title: Apple · Foundation Models framework
sources.note: Native Swift APIs now cover on-device models, guided generation, image understanding and other model providers. Feature availability must be checked at runtime.

sources.title: Apple · What’s new in Foundation Models, WWDC26
sources.note: 2026 additions include vision, context management, semantic search and broader model integration. Our iOS 18 minimum requires a fallback path.

sources.title: Google Research · SensorFM
sources.note: 9 July 2026 research on general representations for wearable signals. A research direction, not a validated drop-in model for Pod sleep stages.

sources.title: Google Research · TimesFM releases and weight licenses
sources.note: August–September 2026 brought TimesFM 3 multivariate forecasting and cloud rollout. Self-hosted 3.0 weights are non-commercial/non-production; weights through 2.5 remain Apache-2.0. Authorized cloud production use has separate terms.

sources.title: Google Research · Anatomy of a personal health agent
sources.note: 30 September 2025 foundational research separates data analysis, domain context and coaching. Useful architecture guidance; not a clinical endorsement of this app.

sources.title: Apple · HealthKit
sources.note: Native, authorized access to personal health records. Data origin and the user’s selected bed side remain essential.

sources.title: Apple · Apple Home
sources.note: Platform context for user-selected Home accessories and scenes. A LAN bridge and real pairing still need qualification.

sources.title: Apple · App Intents
sources.note: Typed actions for Shortcuts and system surfaces. Discovery in a build is distinct from execution on a signed phone.

sources.title: Apple · Meet the Evaluations framework, WWDC26
sources.note: The new framework integrates datasets, quantitative metrics and model-judged criteria with Swift Testing. Use it to qualify the native coach across model and prompt changes; ground numerical truth in application calculations.

updates.title: A morning brief with receipts
updates.pitch: Open the app to one useful observation, the nights behind it, and one optional next step.
updates.example: “Your bedtime was more consistent on 5 recorded nights. See the dates.”
updates.delta: Coach currently answers an explicit request. Add a saved daily brief, delivery preference, and an evidence drawer that links each statement to source dates and computed metrics.
updates.approach: Calculate facts locally, then ask the chosen language model to explain an allowlisted fact set in a typed response. Start with GPT-6.1 Sol and compare Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash. Render a deterministic brief if no cloud sharing is enabled.
updates.dependencies: A versioned evidence record, wake-date/timezone handling, freshness checks and opt-in delivery. Pod presence must remain distinct from measured sleep.
updates.acceptance: Every numerical statement resolves to a stored calculation; missing or sparse nights cause abstention; the same evidence opens on web and iOS. No model may invent a score or a sleep stage.

updates.title: One timeline for Apple Health and your bed
updates.pitch: See Watch sleep, Pod presence, temperature changes and morning feedback on one clearly sourced timeline.
updates.example: Tap a restless interval to see what was recorded, by which device, and what is missing.
updates.delta: The native app already has personal-side Health sync and local comparison. Extend this to an aligned timeline with source filters and explicit overlap resolution; add an opt-in derived-summary path for web parity.
updates.approach: Keep alignment and statistics deterministic. Offer an optional explanation of selected intervals, using only the aggregates the user chooses to share. Use wearable-model research as a future evaluation direction, not as a replacement for source provenance.
updates.dependencies: Signed-device HealthKit validation, per-type consent, a stable personal-side binding, timestamp normalization and clear handling of multiple sleep sources. Web cannot query HealthKit directly.
updates.acceptance: Duplicate sources never double-count time. Users can inspect origin, revoke sharing and remove synchronized summaries. A missing Health sample never becomes a fabricated zero or an inferred stage.

updates.title: A quality and cost center for AI
updates.pitch: Choose a provider with visible evidence, a monthly budget and an understandable privacy setting.
updates.example: “Local only” or “Cloud summaries · chosen provider · usage this month.”
updates.delta: Provider adapters and explicit sharing already exist. Add a repeatable evaluation set, model/version history, usage accounting, a hard request budget and a user-visible comparison of tested results.
updates.approach: Benchmark Sol, Sonnet and Flash on identical de-identified or synthetic cases. Include Gemini 4 Argon as a deeper-reasoning challenger. Test factual grounding, numbers, missing data, misleading notes, response time and total billed tokens. A second model may flag issues but cannot define the ground truth. For the native coach, use Apple’s new Evaluations framework with the same evidence fixtures and measured criteria.
updates.dependencies: Provider keys for live evaluation, expected answers from deterministic calculations, per-provider retention settings and a budget ledger. Cloud data never silently switches to another vendor.
updates.acceptance: All critical fixtures pass with zero fabricated measurements or device commands. The budget blocks further paid calls at its configured ceiling. Publish measured quality/cost results before changing the default.

updates.title: A private coach that works offline
updates.pitch: Ask about your recent pattern on your iPhone without sending your night to a cloud provider.
updates.example: “What changed this week?” answered from local, cited facts even without Wi-Fi.
updates.delta: The server supports a separately installed Ollama model. Add an on-device iOS coach and an editable, deletable memory of user-approved preferences. Keep the same brief and evidence layout on the web.
updates.approach: Use Apple Foundation Models where available, with guided output and a small local evidence index. Use deterministic summaries on unsupported iPhones; a capable Mac/PC can serve the optional local web model. Do not put a large language model on the Pod.
updates.dependencies: OS/device availability checks, a local evaluation suite, explicit memory controls and shared output contracts. Cloud escalation requires a user choice.
updates.acceptance: Airplane-mode tests produce grounded answers on eligible devices; older supported iOS versions render useful fallback summaries. Deleting a memory removes it from subsequent prompts.

updates.title: Personal experiments, one change at a time
updates.pitch: Turn “I think cooler helps” into a small, optional experiment with a clear result and honest uncertainty.
updates.example: Compare your usual setting with a user-selected 1°F change over balanced nights, then review comfort ratings.
updates.delta: The journal already shows habit associations and adaptive comfort learns a bounded offset. Add a guided experiment planner, baseline period, adherence tracking and a review screen.
updates.approach: Let the model explain a predefined protocol. Assign conditions and calculate differences locally, accounting for missed nights and obvious confounders. Use perceived comfort as the primary outcome until other measures are validated.
updates.dependencies: Enough baseline observations, repeat check-ins, user-chosen boundaries, a pause control and qualification of any scheduled temperature changes on real hardware.
updates.acceptance: Only one variable changes per protocol; incomplete data yields an inconclusive result; every change remains reversible. Observational habit patterns are never presented as proof of causation.

updates.title: Predictive comfort before bedtime
updates.pitch: Have the bed approach your chosen temperature at bedtime using its measured heating and cooling behavior.
updates.example: “Start preparation at 9:12 to target 9:30” with a visible forecast and uncertainty range.
updates.delta: Current adaptive comfort adjusts from morning feedback with strict limits. Add a thermal-response forecast, optional room context and a shadow mode that records predictions without controlling the bed.
updates.approach: Start with a simple per-side thermal model. Evaluate TimesFM 2.5 as an offline challenger on a capable local host. A deterministic controller applies validated limits; the LLM only explains the plan. TimesFM 3 self-hosted weights are not a production option under their current license.
updates.dependencies: Real target/actual temperature history, room-temperature data if available, power/presence context and overnight hardware qualification. Performance must be evaluated on held-out nights.
updates.acceptance: Forecast error improves on a simple baseline before activation. Shadow mode, stale-data rejection, manual override, away/alarm guards and rollback all pass physical-device tests.

updates.title: A 20-second spoken morning check-in
updates.pitch: Hold a button, say how the night felt, and review a short check-in before saving it.
updates.example: “Too warm around three; felt okay this morning” becomes editable comfort and restfulness fields.
updates.delta: Replace repetitive form entry with an optional voice path while keeping the existing accessible text form.
updates.approach: Try local dictation first. Offer Gemini 3.8 Live for an explicitly selected conversational mode. Convert speech into typed fields, preserve uncertainty, and require the user to confirm the result.
updates.dependencies: Microphone permission, a visible recording indicator, explicit cloud-audio choice and a clear retention setting. Avoid capturing a sleeping partner with always-on listening.
updates.acceptance: Ambiguous times or negations require correction instead of silent guesses. Cancel discards unsaved audio/transcript data; saving never triggers a device action.

updates.title: Describe a routine; review the exact changes
updates.pitch: Build a schedule in natural language and inspect every affected day, side and setting before applying it.
updates.example: “On weekdays, warm my side at 9:30 and turn it off at 7” becomes a visible schedule diff.
updates.delta: The app already edits schedules and exposes native actions. Add a common web/iOS routine composer that produces the same validated plan, plus a Shortcut entry point for drafting it.
updates.approach: Constrain the model to a schedule schema. Resolve dates and daylight-saving transitions in application code. Apply only a user-confirmed plan through existing authenticated services; keep model tools read-only.
updates.dependencies: Finish and validate the common Routines editor; that work is currently in progress. One-time alarm change/skip/restore is already implemented and locally validated in f5e2b51. Preserve unknown schedule fields, provide rollback, and resolve ambiguous weekdays, sides and overnight intervals.
updates.acceptance: A DST/timezone fixture suite passes. The preview shows all edits and any rejected request. No base movement, schedule write or temperature command occurs during generation.

updates.title: Explain changes and detect bad data
updates.pitch: Distinguish a real shift in your routine from a missing night, an offline sensor or a changed data source.
updates.example: “This week has only two recorded nights, so a trend would be misleading.”
updates.delta: Current analytics preserve unknown values. Add completeness indicators, signal-quality history, comparisons that control for recorded-night count, and a “Why did this change?” drawer.
updates.approach: Use deterministic checks and robust personal baselines for quality signals. Give the model read-only, typed access to calculations and source metadata, so explanations point to exact evidence rather than making arithmetic up.
updates.dependencies: Ingestion timestamps, device/source identifiers, missingness flags and a baseline policy. General wearable foundation models require separate Pod-specific evaluation before any use.
updates.acceptance: Injected outages, clock shifts and duplicate records are identified without becoming health alerts. No diagnosis, apnea detector, readiness score or sleep stage is inferred from presence alone.

updates.title: A wind-down scene that fits your evening
updates.pitch: Connect a chosen bedtime routine with selected lights and bedroom settings, with a clear preview of what will happen.
updates.example: “Wind down” proposes the user’s selected lamp scene and bed preparation time.
updates.delta: The LAN Home bridge foundation already exists. Add scene selection, a readable automation plan, quiet-hour preferences and execution history in the app.
updates.approach: The model drafts a plan from a narrow inventory of user-approved actions. Home and the local scheduler execute fixed, reviewed rules. Remote availability is shown separately from local readiness.
updates.dependencies: Real Home pairing, a supported home hub where required, accessory availability, explicit scene selection and shared-household preferences.
updates.acceptance: Unavailable accessories are reported correctly; duplicate requests do not repeat an action; cancelling the routine stops pending actions. Base movement is excluded from unattended scenes.

updates.title: Position profiles that remember comfort
updates.pitch: Save your preferred reading or resting position and compare how comfortable it felt over time.
updates.example: “Your saved reading position: head 24°, feet 10°” with preview, explicit Move and persistent Stop.
updates.delta: Head/feet sliders, presets and a reported-position view already exist. Add user-named profiles, feedback history and optional recommendations based on the positions the user has actually tried.
updates.approach: Use a small transparent ranking model for preference learning; use an LLM only to explain the evidence. Recommendations are drafts. Whole-bed movement remains a deliberate physical action.
updates.dependencies: Verify BLE telemetry, limits, calibration, motion and Stop on the owner’s stock Pod/base first. Account for partner presence and shared-bed preferences.
updates.acceptance: Reported position stays separate from requested position. Stale telemetry blocks movement; Stop cancels pending movement. The product makes no snoring, apnea or therapeutic claims.

updates.title: An optional photo-assisted context journal
updates.pitch: Reduce logging effort by extracting visible text from a caffeine label or travel itinerary, then letting you correct it.
updates.example: A label photo suggests a product name and printed caffeine amount; the user supplies portion and time.
updates.delta: The journal currently uses checkboxes and text. Add a small attachment flow with highlighted evidence, confidence and editable fields, linked to the night it may help explain.
updates.approach: Prefer on-device OCR/image understanding where available; evaluate a selected multimodal cloud model only with consent. Treat text in images as data, never instructions. Do not infer consumed dose, meal calories or medical implications from appearance.
updates.dependencies: Image privacy controls, attachment deletion, time/portion confirmation, and a richer journal schema shared by web and iOS.
updates.acceptance: Every extracted fact highlights its source text. Unreadable fields stay empty. Cloud sharing and photo retention are optional, and extracted context cannot directly change the bed.
